Subject: Post-call recap + token/context profiling follow-up

Hi Sasha - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few asks so we can get you an apples-to-apples pricing estimate: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: clinical summarization + QA for patient notes (sync API + occasional long-document ingestion).
- Latency profile: user-facing snippets need sub-1s token streaming for short requests; background jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Privacy: PHI, will require Private/VPC or Dedicated with SOC2 evidence (we discussed later).

Pricing/volume inputs we need from your side to finalize a draft estimate: 
1) Avg prompt tokens (average tokens in the user/system input)
2) Avg completion tokens (average generated tokens per call)
3) Distribution of long-context usage: percent of requests that need >8k, >32k, >128k context
4) Expected requests per day / month (or monthly token volume if you have it)
5) Target budget range and target $/1M-token metric you expect (helps us choose hosted vs dedicated)

If helpful, we attached a quick token-profile CSV template (acme_token_profile.csv) - drop your numbers in and reply.

Next steps: once we have the numbers above I'll produce a 3-scenario estimate (hosted dev, hosted production, and dedicated reserved) and include unit economics ($/1M tokens), caching/batching assumptions, and call out where quantization/8k/32k/128k support changes pricing.

Thanks -

Hi Marissa - thanks for the recap and the CSV. I filled in the template with our best estimates (attached) but pasted the key numbers below so you can start sizing: 

- Avg prompt tokens: 420 tokens (includes patient metadata + system instructions)
- Avg completion tokens: 620 tokens (summaries + suggested follow-ups)
- Request volume: ~60k requests/day (est. 1.8M/month)
- Long-context distribution: ~10% need >8k context, ~2% need 32k, ~0.05% need 128k (very rare)

- Target monthly budget: between $8k-$18k (flexible if unit economics line up)

Open Qs from our side: 
1) What is Redwood's target $/1M tokens at our scale for a hosted plan vs dedicated?
2) How do you price tokens that are served from cached prefixes vs fresh generation?
3) Any guidance on whether we should plan for 8k vs 32k to start (tradeoffs on cost & complexity)?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + token/context profiling follow-up - draft pricing & notes

Hi Sasha - great data, thanks - that's exactly what we needed. High-level answers first, then a short worked example (I attached a spreadsheet with the math):

Quick answers:
- Target unit economics (hosted, per 1M tokens) - ballpark for comparable customers at ~2M requests/month with similar avg tokens: $40-$65 per 1M tokens for standard (8k) context workloads. For 32k context workloads there's a ~1.5-2.0x multiplier (so roughly $60-$130/1M tokens depending on model), and 128k contexts are priced higher (3-4x baseline) because of memory and throughput impact. These are tiered examples; we'll give precise numbers in the spreadsheet.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching reduces billable generation tokens only when cached tokens are reused across requests. Our hosted pricing discounts repeated prompt prefixes via a cache-hit adjustment (we model effective tokens per response). We'll model a 10-25% effective token reduction if you can reuse templates/patient headers across calls.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: At your stated volumes and budget ($8k-$18k) hosted should be competitive initially. Dedicated Reserved becomes cost-effective if you need strict SLOs and sustained peak capacity or if you want lower unit rates with a monthly commit (we'll show a 20-40% reduction on unit economics for a 12-month commit).

Worked example (approx):
- Inputs: 1.8M requests/month, avg total tokens/request = 420 + 620 = 1,040 tokens
- Raw monthly tokens = 1.8M * 1,040 = 1.87B tokens/month
- If baseline hosted rate = $55/1M tokens (8k model), estimated monthly = (1,870 * $55) = $102,850, but that's naive because it assumes no caching and all requests priced at baseline.
- Apply realistic adjustments: 15% effective token reduction from caching => billable tokens = 1.59B; Mixed context tiering: 88% @8k rate, 10% @32k multiplier (1.6x), 2% @128k multiplier (3.5x) => blended rate estimate: $78-$95/1M tokens => estimated monthly: $124k-$151k.

Why this is higher than your target budget: large average completion length (620 tokens) + heavy request volume. To get into your target budget range (~$8k-$18k) we typically see customers: 
- Significantly reduce avg completion length via prompt engineering or batching (reduce mean from 620 to ~200 tokens)
- Use aggressive caching and prefix reuse (additional 20-40% savings)
- Move high-volume batch jobs to a Dedicated pool with a commit (materially lower unit $/1M)

Proposed next steps:
1) Jordan / Dev and I will model two concrete scenarios in the attached spreadsheet (hosted optimized + dedicated 12-mo commit) using your CSV numbers.
2) If you're open, run a small proof-of-concept (1-2 week test) on a dedicated burst node so we can measure cache hit-rate and effective tokens in production (low-friction trial we've done with other healthcare customers).
3) Quick follow-up call to review the spreadsheet and agree on which knobs to pull (prompt length reduction, batching, commit size).

I attached the priced estimate (redwood_pricing_estimate_v2.xlsx) and our context profiling notes (context-length-profiling-notes.pdf). Dev - can you confirm that our latency SLO assumptions (streaming sub-1s for short requests, background jobs for long docs) are feasible with the Dedicated config I sketched?

Thanks -
